verdict.rationale: Browserbase documents session observability (rich logs, live view, session replay) and registrable webhooks that POST to your endpoint when subscribed events occur, which covers monitoring and failure alerting for browser jobs. Nothing in the evidence shows built-in data-quality validation, and there is no documented job-performance metrics view. missing for 10: data-quality validation of extracted output, explicit job-performance metrics/dashboards, documented failure-specific webhook event types, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, I can monitor job performance, validate data quality, and receive alerts when something fails

citations.quote: best-in-class observability (rich logs, live view, and session replay)
Browserbase webhooks send an HTTP POST to an endpoint you own as soon as a subscribed event happens, so you don't have to poll the API for status changes.
You can manage endpoints from Settings as well as through the SDK.
Create, control, and observe browser sessions programmatically.
